intro.title: color-scheme
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage that automatically adapts its color scheme to match your system's light or dark mode preference. You will learn the core concept of the CSS `color-scheme` property, which allows you to control how the browser renders default UI elements like form controls and scrollbars. The main technology involved is CSS, using this property to ensure visual consistency. By the end, you'll understand how to implement `color-scheme` to create a more seamless user experience across different system settings.
intro.usecase: The color-scheme property is essential for creating accessible applications that respect user preferences across operating systems and browsers. Developers use it to ensure form controls, dropdown menus, and scrollbars automatically match the user's chosen light or dark mode in settings panels, admin dashboards, and data visualization tools. This eliminates manual theming for native UI components in complex interfaces like analytics platforms or content management systems, providing consistent visual experiences while reducing development overhead.
